lim.title: Interactive whiteboard detected
lim.description: Whiteboard mode enlarges text and makes the charts lighter.

toast.componentsAdded: {n, plural, one {# component added} other {# components added}}
toast.forked: Saved as a new project: “{name}”. The original lab stays as it was.
toast.stopBeforeLab: Stop the measurement before changing experiment.
toast.stopBeforeComponents: Stop the measurement before changing the components.
toast.stopBeforeDelete: Stop the measurement before deleting the project.
toast.keepOneChart: At least one chart must stay visible.
toast.phoneDisconnected: Phone sensors turned off during the measurement. The data collected has been saved.
toast.arduinoDisconnected: Arduino disconnected during the measurement. The data collected has been saved.
toast.noFirmware: Arduino responds, but it doesn’t have the MosaicusNeo firmware. Upload it with the Arduino IDE.
toast.oldFirmware: Arduino has firmware v{fw}: update it to v{need}.
toast.btSetup: Configuring the Bluetooth module: name “MosaicusNeo”, 115200 baud…
toast.btNoReply: The Bluetooth module didn’t respond. Check TXD → D0 and RXD ← D1 (with the voltage divider), that the module’s LED is blinking and that no phone is connected, then try again.
toast.bleConfigured: BLE module configured: it is now called “MosaicusNeo”. Unplug the cable, power Arduino and choose “Bluetooth LE” → “MosaicusNeo” (on iPhone use the Bluefy browser). If the name doesn’t appear, look for HMSoft, BT05 or HC-08.
toast.hc06Configured: HC-06 module configured: it is now called “MosaicusNeo”. Pair it in the phone’s Bluetooth settings (PIN 1234).
toast.fwOutdatedLoad: Firmware out of date: upload mosaicusneo_firmware.ino v{v} with the Arduino IDE.
toast.stopBeforeTest: Stop the measurement before the test.
toast.outputsNeedFw: Display, LED and buzzer require firmware v1.2. Update it following the “Guide”.
toast.outputsRejected: Arduino rejected the display, LED and buzzer.
toast.outputsRejectedWhy: Arduino rejected the display, LED and buzzer: {why}.
toast.testSent: Test sent. Check: the LED changes color, the buzzer sounds, the display shows “HELLO”.
toast.testNoReply: Arduino didn’t respond to the test.
toast.cfgNoReply: Arduino isn’t responding to the configuration. Disconnect it and connect it again.
toast.accessoriesError: Accessories (display, LED, buzzer, button, SD card): {why}.
toast.cfgFwOutdated: Firmware out of date: configuring the components requires v{v}. You’ll find the steps in the “Guide”.
toast.needFirmware: {what}: firmware v{need} is required (Arduino has v{fw}). Update it with the Arduino IDE.
toast.notStarted: The measurement didn’t start. Check the components’ wiring and try again.
toast.connectUsbFirst: Connect Arduino with the USB cable first.
toast.stopBeforeModule: Stop the measurement before configuring the module.
toast.moduleFwOutdated: Firmware out of date: configuring the module requires v{v}.
toast.componentAddedHint: In the “Wiring” tab you’ll find the updated diagram and how to connect it.
toast.keyBlocked: Button pressed, but the measurement can’t start: {why}
toast.keyIdle: Button pressed: Arduino is connected, but the measurement can’t start right now.
toast.saved: Measurement saved in the Notebook · {n, plural, one {# reading} other {# readings}}.
toast.noDistance: No valid distance: can’t set the origin.
toast.originSet: Origin set at {d} m from the sensor.
toast.stopBeforeSend: Stop the measurement before saving a range.
toast.noValidData: The range contains no valid data. Select another one.
toast.needThreePoints: At least 3 valid points are needed. Select a longer range.
toast.interpolated: The values of the other components are interpolated at the same instants.
toast.rangeAdded: Range added to Analysis · {n, plural, one {# point} other {# points}}.
toast.rangeAddedInterpolated: Range added to Analysis · {n, plural, one {# point} other {# points}}. The values of the other components are interpolated at the same instants.
toast.noGps: No points with a GPS position to export.
toast.stopBeforeOpen: Stop the measurement before opening another one from the Notebook.
toast.cannotOpen: Can’t open the measurement: its experiment or project no longer exists.
toast.opened: Opened “{name}”. If you change the components’ options, the data is recalculated.
toast.pinsMoved: {list}: moved to make room for {name}. Rewire them as shown in the Wiring tab.
toast.btPlug: Now connect the module’s TXD wire to D0. Arduino waits for the module to answer for about 30 seconds.
toast.btUnplugFirst: Arduino didn’t receive “Configure”. Unplug the TXD → D0 wire (on the Uno it drowns out the USB cable’s commands) and press “Configure” again: the app will tell you when to plug it back in.
toast.deniedPhone: Sensor permission denied. Allow it in the browser’s site settings, then try again.
toast.deniedDevice: The browser blocked access to the device. Allow it in the site settings, then try again.

cfgErr.DOPPIO: pin already used by another component

err.CARD: the card isn’t responding. Is it fully inserted? Check the MISO (D12), MOSI (D11), SCK (D13) and CS wires
err.FAT32: the card isn’t formatted as FAT32. Format it as FAT32 on the computer (cards over 32 GB come formatted as exFAT)
err.FILE: the file can’t be created: the card’s root folder is full. Move or delete some files
err.NOOUT: Arduino doesn’t know it has the SD card: try “Prepare Arduino” again

sd.stopBefore: Stop the measurement before preparing the recording.
sd.needFirmware: The SD card and the button require firmware v1.5 (Arduino has v{fw}). Update it with the Arduino IDE.
sd.addFirst: Add the SD card to the components first.
sd.notSavedToast: Arduino didn’t save the configuration. Update the firmware to v1.5 and try again.
sd.testNoReply: Arduino didn’t respond to the card test.
sd.testNoReplyToast: Arduino didn’t respond to the SD card test.
sd.howButton: press the button to start and again to stop
sd.howPower: it records from when you switch it on to when you switch it off
sd.ready: Ready. Unplug the cable, power Arduino with a power bank and {how}.
sd.readyCard: Ready · {size} card. Unplug the cable, power Arduino with a power bank and {how}.
sd.readyToast: Arduino is ready to record on the SD card.
sd.noReadings: “{file}”: no readings (was the recording too short?).
sd.unknownProject: “{file}” comes from a project this device doesn’t know: sensors rebuilt with default options (calibrations included).
sd.badRows: “{file}”: {n, plural, one {# incomplete row discarded} other {# incomplete rows discarded}}.
sd.imported: {n, plural, one {Recording imported} other {# recordings imported}} into the Notebook.

workbench.exported: {n, plural, one {Panel exported to Excel.} other {# panels exported to Excel.}}

live.hintPhone: Open the app on the phone: computers usually don’t have these sensors
live.gpsHint: Outdoors, open sky: from 30 s to a few minutes
live.hintDs18b20: Check the 4.7 kΩ resistor between DATA and 5V
live.hintSonar: A flat target between 5 cm and 3 m is needed

cloud.offline: You’re offline. Syncing resumes when the connection is back.
cloud.adopted: {n, plural, one {1 item created on this device has been added} other {# items created on this device have been added}} to your account.
cloud.deleteUnavailable: Account deletion isn’t active on the server yet. Write to the address given in the privacy notice.

auth.emailNotConfirmed: First confirm your email address with the link we sent you.
auth.alreadyRegistered: An account with this email already exists. Use “Sign in”.
auth.passwordShort: The password must be at least 6 characters long.
auth.rateLimit: Too many attempts: try again in a few minutes.

combine.cannot: These measurements can’t be combined (saved by an older version).
combine.noSd: SD card recordings don’t carry the real time of day, so they can’t be lined up with other measurements.
combine.noOverlap: The two measurements don’t overlap in time: start both before stopping either.
combine.name: {a} + {b}
combine.doneHint: Both measurements on one time axis, corrected for the drift between the two Arduino clocks. It’s in the Notebook.

diag.noReply: Arduino isn’t responding to the configuration
diag.d0Blocked: Arduino isn’t receiving commands from the USB cable
diag.d0BlockedHint: The Bluetooth module on D0 drowns out the USB cable: unplug the TXD → D0 wire while you use the cable, or connect over Bluetooth.
